Evelyn K: hi all, onboarding q — setting up CI that hits the API for smoke tests. should we use a sandbox key, or can we use hosted keys scoped to the repo? also, security requires a stable IP to whitelist.

Maya R (DevEx): welcome! :wave: Use sandbox keys for dev/CI smoke tests by default. Hosted keys are reserved for staging/prod. For CI, prefer ephemeral keys tied to the job so they expire if leaked. See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/dev/ci-keys

Evelyn K: ephemeral keys — how do those work? can GH Actions get one automatically?

InfraBot: Ephemeral CI keys are supported. Create a service account token via Console -> Service Accounts, then mint short-lived keys (TTL up to 8h) via our token service: POST /v1/service_accounts/{id}/tokens.

Raj - SRE: for the IP whitelist issue, option A: run CI runners inside our dev VPC (egress 34.200.10.5) and ask security to whitelist that IP. Option B: use the org devproxy forwarder (egress 35.189.77.9). Both require an infra ticket.

Sofia - Security: if you request whitelist, include repo name, runner IDs, start/end time, and contact. Temporary whitelists are preferred.

Evelyn K: thanks. last bit: our CI creates ~100 parallel jobs for fast feedback. worried about 429s — is there a per-key concurrency limit we should plan for?

Maya R (DevEx): sandbox keys have default lower quotas. InfraBot posted defaults earlier. For parallel CI, best practice: use multiple ephemeral keys (one per runner) to distribute load, and respect Retry-After headers. Also add exponential backoff + jitter to test harness.

InfraBot: Current sandbox defaults = 60 req/min per key and 8 concurrent streaming connections per key. For bulk CI, request a temporary quota increase or org-level quota from infra and include expected concurrency.

Raj - SRE: example GH Actions step to mint a short-lived token and set as secret (pseudo):
```
- name: Mint RW token
  run: |
    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.SA_ADMIN }}" \
      https://console.redwood.ai/v1/service_accounts/sa-123/tokens -d '{"ttl":3600}' \
      | jq -r .token > rw_token
    echo "RW_TOKEN=$(cat rw_token)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
Then use RW_TOKEN in requests.

Maya R (DevEx): and monitor X-RateLimit-* headers in CI logs so you can detect approaching limits. If you see Retry-After, pause and back off. We can help size the quota if you paste the expected RPS.

Evelyn K: perfect, i'll prototype with ephemeral tokens + smaller parallelism and open an infra ticket if we need higher quotas. thanks y'all! :raised_hands:
